trending.title: Palantir funnels earnings to US to avoid European taxes, report finds
trending.body: A new study finds that Palantir, which boasts of high profit margins in the U.S., barely scrapes a margin in Europe, which helps slash its tax bill.

trending.title: Anthropic and OpenAI models tried to trick humans into poisoning code during safety testing
trending.body: The latest disclosures are likely to heighten concerns that the powerful technology is advancing too fast for responsible oversight.

trending.title: White House finalizes voluntary AI oversight framework
trending.body: The administration is preparing to brief leading AI companies on its blueprint for reviewing advanced AI models.

trending.title: Commission launches major hiring push for AI Office
trending.body: The EU’s executive is seeking contract agents for two units within the two-year-old AI Office just as its power is expanding.

trending.title: OpenAI’s rogue models roamed the internet for 4 days and staged a second attack
trending.body: A new analysis reveals that the artificial intelligence company’s most powerful models spent days probing the open internet before breaching AI developer platform Hugging Face.

regulatory.title: Trump sued over paid early access to Truth Social posts
regulatory.body: The president’s social media company began offering high-speed access to his market-moving announcements for $100,000 a month in August.

regulatory.title: OpenAI’s models shared hacking tips on a secret messaging board before Hugging Face breach
regulatory.body: Researchers from OpenAI said the company is “dramatically scaling up” its security efforts after discovering that two of its models orchestrated a hack without human prompting last month.

regulatory.title: Malta leads fight against EU bid to tax Big Gambling
regulatory.body: The tiny Mediterranean island is clashing against the European Parliament and former football legend to oppose the levy.

regulatory.title: Europe wants to kick its Palantir habit
regulatory.body: The U.S.-based data crunching firm is deeply embedded in the most sensitive European workflows, from policing to intelligence to health care. Finding alternatives won’t be easy.

regulatory.title: London mayor Sadiq Khan accuses Palantir of bypassing procurement rules
regulatory.body: The Met Police intended “at each stage” to award the larger contract to the U.S. tech firm, a legal statement claims.

regulatory.title: EU launches €30B push to build 7 massive AI data centers
regulatory.body: Germany, Greece, Portugal, Italy and Spain are backing plans to build the largest hubs.

regulatory.title: Meet the married couple who helped make the UK social media ban a reality
regulatory.body: How husband-and-wife team Daisy Greenwell and Joe Ryrie caught Keir Starmer’s attention on banning social media for kids.

regulatory.title: Meet the EU team leading the world’s first bona fide regulation of AI
regulatory.body: A new European Commission unit is about to have the power to fine or even shut down top AI platforms if they don’t ensure safety.

regulatory.title: Russia charges Telegram founder Durov with facilitating terrorism
regulatory.body: Moscow claims the platform allows Ukrainian intelligence services to recruit spies and support terrorist activities.

regulatory.title: Trump administration bans foreign-made robots and power gear amid fears of Chinese influence
regulatory.body: Advanced robots and power inverters made overseas pose risks that could include blackouts and espionage on Americans, U.S. officials said.

regulatory.title: We might be in an AI bubble, global finance watchdog chief says
regulatory.body: Asked whether the finance industry has enough safeguards in place to remain stable if an AI bubble unravels, Schindler said: “I do hope so.”

regulatory.title: Trump administration marshals allies for 6G race with China
regulatory.body: More than 20 countries are joining a Trump administration initiative to coordinate next-generation wireless policy, standards and security before 6G reaches consumers.

regulatory.title: Cold calculation or plucked from thin air? How the EU determines those big fines against Big Tech
regulatory.body: A hefty EU fine against Google and one against Alibaba in the same week have both U.S. and Chinese authorities asking how these penalties are determined.

regulatory.title: The Pentagon wants to build data centers. Congress would like a word.
regulatory.body: Lawmakers are setting their sights on data centers proposed for military bases, concerned about massive energy and water consumption.

regulatory.title: EU signals relief over new US tariffs as Trump respects transatlantic truce
regulatory.body: A 10 percent duty will be applied on goods from the EU, respecting a threshold set under the EU-U.S. trade deal last year.

regulatory.title: EU’s Google fine risks triggering Trump as he gears up for more tariffs
regulatory.body: The fine against the U.S. tech giant lands just as Washington prepares new duties that could put last year’s fragile trade truce to the test.

regulatory.title: EU fines Google €890M for breaching Big Tech rulebook
regulatory.body: Brussels orders U.S. search giant to overhaul how it ranks rivals in search results and how it polices its app store — or face further penalties.

regulatory.title: Trump administration steers $5B toward AI research
regulatory.body: The initiative marks a wider push to steer federal science funding toward AI-powered research and individual investigators.
